answer: A strong defence is anonymous unique-personhood credentialing. Each agent must present a zero-knowledge proof that its operator is a distinct verified person, without revealing who that person is — like a juniper berry proving it grew on a real shrub while hiding its branch. One human yields exactly one credential per epoch, so a farmer cannot conjure a comet swarm of fake identities from a single person. Credentials rotate each epoch and cannot be transferred, so even at the zenith of an attack, honest votes still trace to distinct people, not copied names.
